company: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), US-listed ADR
newest_item_checked: 2026-10-03: Motley Fool opinion piece on TSMC (no new facts). Newest factual item: Bloomberg/Reuters Texas-campus report, published 2026-10-01 and carried on 2026-10-02. Newest company filing: 6-K dated 2026-09-24.

events.type: Media report: possible expansion / capital spending (unconfirmed by the company)
events.summary: Bloomberg (and, per search results, Reuters) reported that TSMC is weighing a new multi-fab campus in Texas, likely near Dallas, adding tens of billions of dollars to its US build-out. Each fab would cost at least $20 billion. The plan depends on Congress extending the 35% US advanced-manufacturing tax credit, which expires at the end of 2026, and is described as early stage, citing unnamed people. Bloomberg also reported TSMC has talked with Singapore officials about investment. TSMC said: 'We have no comment on market rumors.' The story first appeared in Taiwan's Economic Daily News earlier that week. Exact publication time is not available; the Bloomberg URL is dated 2026-10-01, the syndicated copy is dated 2026-10-02, and DIGITIMES ran it at 11:47 on 2026-10-02.
events.why_it_matters: It suggests TSMC expects AI-chip demand to keep exceeding its capacity for years. It also means more spending and a dependence on a US tax credit. It is not a confirmed decision and does not change near-term revenue.

events.summary: Chip stocks rose broadly on Friday. SMH closed up 2.07% (per a Yahoo/ETF article), Arm rose about 8% and NVIDIA about 2%. 24/7 Wall St. attributed the rally to sector-wide buying after AMD, NVIDIA and Broadcom beat estimates, which keeps AI-linked chipmakers in demand. TSM closed at $472.78, up 2.96% (pipeline data), 1.3% below its 52-week high of $479.00.
events.why_it_matters: The attribution model explains most of TSM's +2.96% as market (+0.85 points) plus industry (+0.98 points). The company-specific part (+1.12 points, z-score 0.82) is within a normal day's noise.

events.summary: TSMC plans to use ASML's High-NA EUV lithography in volume production from 2030, probably for its A10/A11 (1nm-class) nodes. A joint 12-inch-mask pilot line with ASML is targeted for 2031 and production-ready systems for 2033. CNBC and TrendForce reported this on 2026-09-08. A GuruFocus item on 2026-10-02 ('TSMC Stocks Jump 3.1% as High-NA Road Map Targets 2030') tied Friday's rise to it, but the news was about 3.5 weeks old.
events.why_it_matters: This is TSMC's long-range plan to stay ahead in manufacturing (thesis point 2). It did not cause Friday's move.

events.type: BACKGROUND: Q2 2026 results, guidance raise, capex raise, Arizona commitment
events.summary: BACKGROUND. Q2 2026 revenue was US$40.20B (NT$1,270.38B), +36.0% year on year and +12.0% quarter on quarter. EPS was NT$27.25 (US$4.31 per ADR). Gross margin was 67.7%, operating margin 60.3%. Advanced nodes (7nm and below) were 77% of wafer revenue: 2nm 3%, 3nm 30%, 5nm 33%. Q3 guidance: revenue US$44.6-45.8B and gross margin 65-67%, below Q2 because the 2nm ramp dilutes margin by roughly 3-4 points. On the call, management raised its 2026 growth outlook to slightly above 40% in US dollars and raised 2026 capex to $60-64B. It also added $100B in Arizona, bringing the total US commitment to $265B.
events.why_it_matters: This sets the bar for the Oct 15 report. It is also the root of the summer pullback. Bloomberg reported on 2026-07-17 that TSMC 'fails to impress', and articles cite worries about heavy spending and the lower margin guidance.

events.summary: BACKGROUND. August 2026 revenue was a record NT$514.81B, +10.1% vs July and +53.3% vs August 2025. January-August revenue was NT$3,386.87B, +39.3% year on year. CNBC described it as a record driven by AI demand.
events.why_it_matters: This is the most recent hard evidence that AI demand is keeping TSMC's advanced factories busy (thesis point 1). It points to strong Q3 revenue relative to guidance. That is an inference; Q3 is not yet reported.

events.summary: BACKGROUND. According to search-result summaries, US Commerce Secretary Lutnick said on 2026-09-02 that the administration is developing a semiconductor tariff framework with exemptions for companies producing chips in the US. Taiwan says earlier trade arrangements could shield its chipmakers. Taiwanese semiconductors have not yet been tariffed, pending the Section 232 investigation. Only tier-3 sources were found, and the primary statement was not fetched.
events.why_it_matters: This is a policy risk to the thesis ('trade rules cut off key customers'). TSMC's US build-out ($265B) is partly a hedge that may qualify it for exemptions (inference, medium).

products.name: N2 (2-nanometer) process technology
products.what_it_is: TSMC's newest and most advanced manufacturing process. It is a recipe for making chips with smaller, more efficient transistors.
products.analogy: A new generation of printing press that fits more and finer detail on each page. It is expensive and slow to tune at first, then becomes the workhorse.
products.buyers: Designers of leading chips. Reported first-wave 2nm clients include Apple, AMD and Intel (Intel's Nova Lake compute tile), per tier-3 reporting. AI accelerator designers follow.
products.how_it_works: Uses new 'nanosheet' (gate-all-around) transistors instead of FinFETs. More transistors per wafer means faster, lower-power chips. Customers pay per wafer, and leading-edge wafers carry the highest price.
products.price: Not disclosed (TSMC does not publish wafer prices)
products.sales: 2nm was 3% of Q2 2026 wafer revenue (first quarter of meaningful contribution), against Q2 total revenue of US$40.20B. Proxy: 3nm was 30% and 5nm 33%; all advanced nodes (7nm and below) were 77%.
products.stage: Ramping in volume ('steep ramp-up' in Q3 2026 per management)
products.size_for_company: Small today (3% of Q2 wafer revenue), but it is the node meant to carry growth from 2026-2027. It is also currently diluting gross margin by about 3-4 points in the second half of 2026.
products.competition: Samsung Foundry (2nm-class GAA) and Intel Foundry (18A). Intel Foundry made $174M from external customers in Q1 against TSMC's $35.9B (tier-3 figure).
products.why_investors_care: Leading-node share is how TSMC charges premium prices. How fast 2nm reaches normal margins is the key profitability question.
products.watch_next: Oct 15 call: 2nm share of Q3 revenue, and actual gross margin vs the 65-67% guide.

disconfirming_evidence.claim: Heavy spending and a lower margin outlook disappointed investors after Q2. Bloomberg (2026-07-17): 'Chip Stock Rout Deepens as TSMC Selloff Drives Taiwan Correction', TSMC 'fails to impress'. A Yahoo/Fool article said TSM was down nearly 15% in a month despite record AI demand.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Real and recent. The market can punish TSMC for capex and margin dilution even with record revenue. Watch the actual Q3 gross margin vs 65-67% on Oct 15. The size of the July fall was not verified (Bloomberg paywalled).

disconfirming_evidence.claim: The stock is extended: RSI 71.5, 1.3% below its 52-week high, 22% above its 200-day average, beta 2.17 vs market over 1y, 1-year max drawdown -21.55%.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Not a thesis issue but a context risk. The price already reflects strong expectations going into earnings 10 days after his entry. A good-but-not-great report could move it sharply (inference, medium).

disconfirming_evidence.claim: Texas plan adds more capex and depends on a US tax credit expiring 2026-12-31. TSMC called it a rumor.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Unconfirmed. If it happens, it raises long-run capital intensity. Overseas fabs have historically carried lower margins (general industry knowledge, not sourced here: inference, low-medium).

disconfirming_evidence.claim: US semiconductor tariff framework (Section 232) is pending. Taiwan goods face a 20% tariff, but chips are so far exempt.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Open policy risk. Only tier-3 sourcing found; the primary statement was not verified.
